selected_evidence.summary: The account exists with UID 1000, home /home/appworker, and shell /bin/bash before and after reboot.

selected_evidence.requirement: Set login-session open-file limit to 8,192 and process limit to 256
selected_evidence.summary: The persistent PAM limits file sets both limits, and fresh login sessions report soft/hard nofile=8192 and nproc=256 before and after reboot.

selected_evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel
selected_evidence.summary: CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 were unchanged.

Healthy baseline and effective task state were captured; systemd acknowledged the safe reboot; boot ID changed from 4d842549-003e-4f78-bb26-12732f129e58 to fdf539bb-fc65-4e2d-a99f-65fd2e4fbea2; afterward the system was running, sshd was active, and the account and limits had recovered.

commands.command: useradd -m -s /bin/bash appworker && getent passwd appworker && test -d /home/appworker && stat -c 'home_owner=%U:%G mode=%a' /home/appworker

umask 022; printf '%s\n' '# Resource limits for appworker login sessions' 'appworker - nofile 8192' 'appworker - nproc 256' > /etc/security/limits.d/60-appworker.conf; chown root:root /etc/security/limits.d/60-appworker.conf; chmod 0644 /etc/security/limits.d/60-appworker.conf; cat /etc/security/limits.d/60-appworker.conf; stat -c 'owner=%U:%G mode=%a' /etc/security/limits.d/60-appworker.conf
commands.stdout:
# Resource limits for appworker login sessions
appworker - nofile 8192
appworker - nproc 256
owner=root:root mode=644
